overview: Two categories of peripheral nerves, distinguished by where they originate from the central nervous system.
genZNote: Cranial nerves: direct lines straight out of the brain. Spinal nerves: lines that branch off along the spinal cord.

aspects.label: Origin
aspects.valueA: Arise directly from the brain (brainstem mostly).

aspects.label: Fibre Type
aspects.valueA: Can be sensory, motor, or mixed, depending on the specific nerve.
aspects.valueB: Almost all are mixed nerves, carrying both sensory and motor fibres.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueB: Sciatic nerve, formed from spinal nerve roots in the lower back.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Humans have exactly 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves — both frequently tested counts.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cranial = from the cranium (skull/brain). Spinal = from the spinal cord.
overlay.commonMisconception: Not all cranial nerves are purely sensory or purely motor — several, like the vagus nerve, carry both sensory and motor fibres, similar to spinal nerves.
